chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Mansur bin al-Abbas, from Ali bin Asbaat, from a man from our companions called Abdul Rahman bin Sinan, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), when a man came to him and gave him thirty dinars to perform Hajj on behalf of Ismail. He did not leave out anything from the Umrah to the Hajj except that he stipulated it upon him, to the extent that he stipulated upon him that he should perform Sa'i from the valley of Muhassar. Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'O this man! When you do this, it will be a Hajj for Ismail with whatever he spent from his wealth, and for you will be nine (times as much) with what you exhaust yourself from your body.'

key_terms.وَادِي مُحَسِّر: Valley of Muhassar (a specific location in Mecca relevant to Sa'i)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for performing Hajj on behalf of someone else?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distribution of spiritual rewards in Hajj al-Ni'bah (Hajj on behalf of another), establishing that the financial expenditure is credited to the principal while the performer receives a ninefold reward for their physical exertion. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the merit of the agent's labor and endurance, distinguishing it from the mere fulfillment of the obligation. The specific mention of Sa'i from Wadi Muhassir underscores the detailed adherence to ritual geography and tradition in Imam al-Sadiq's teachings.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from a man from our companions called Abdul Rahman Bin Sinan who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, when a man came over to him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> gave him thirty Dinars to perform Hajj with it on behalf of Ismail, and he<sup>asws</sup> did not leave anything from the Umra to the Hajj, except that he<sup>asws</sup> stipulated upon him, to the extent that he<sup>asws</sup> stipulated upon him that he should be walking briskly from the valley of Muhassar. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O you! When you do this, it would be a Hajj for Ismail with whatever is spent from his wealth, and for you would be nine (times as much) with what you exhaust yourself from your body’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Mansur ibn al-‘Abbas from Ali ibn Asbat from a man of our people called ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Sinan who has said the following:

“Once I was in the presence of abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when someone came, and he (the Imam) gave him thirty dinar to perform al-Hajj for ‘Isma‘il, and set a condition to perform all acts of al-Hajj and al-‘Umrah, even walking in manner of running in Muhassar valley. He (the Imam) then said, ‘O so and so, if you did as the conditions require you to do, it will be al-Hajj for ‘Isma‘il that you are paid for, and you will have nine times over for tiring your body.”’
